title: [observability] A guardrail's raise hold survives a loop restart: a figure out at the loop's first reading takes its out-since from the hourly samples
prompt:
Spawn, objective 192 [observability] (the lead, 2026-11-15, from rev-e's live finding of 2026-11-14 23:4x; rev-e; reviewer rev-g): a guardrail's raise hold survives a loop restart.

Why. No guardrail_out_of_range alert has ever fired on live, although figures sit out of range all day. At 2026-11-14 23:3x live's /api/core-lines said:
- storage.days_left: 8, against 180 or more;
- storage.leaked_test_schemas: 1239, against 200 or less. The hourly samples had it over 200 all evening.
spawn_alerts holds no guardrail_out_of_range row, open or cleared, yet the loop read the figures every ~5 min ("alerts: core lines read").
The cause:
- The raise hold (SPAWN_GUARDRAIL_RAISE_SECS, 2 h) is counted in the loop's memory (guardrail_out: figure → out since). A restarted loop counts again from its first reading, and adopts only alerts that are already open.
- Every deploy restarts the loop. Live recorded 37 deploy.finished in the 24 h before 23:4x, and almost every gap was under 2 h.
- So the hold never completed, and every guardrail alert, 176's and 182's included, was silent.

Base: live main 6796e8c6 (the rewritten history).

Read first:
- crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts/guardrails.rs: start_guardrails, guardrail_events, the module doc;
- crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines.rs: reading;
- crates/spawn-cli/src/core_lines_sample.rs: Sampler, SPAWN_CORE_LINES_SAMPLE_SECS;
- crates/spawn-postgres/src/host.rs: HOST_CORE_LINES.

What changes:
(1) The loop's first guardrail reading carries the hourly samples: serve::core_lines::reading_with_samples(since).
   - It is the same reading, plus store.host_core_lines(since) on the same connection, as `recent_samples` ([{at_ms, values}], oldest first), or `recent_samples_error`.
   - since = now − the raise hold − two sample periods.
   - It is not part of GET /api/core-lines, and later readings are as before.
(2) At that reading, each figure that is out of range, not stale and has no count yet takes its out-since from those samples (guardrails::out_since): the time of the oldest sample in the newest unbroken run of samples out of the figure's current range, with that run reaching the loop's start.
   - What ends the run: a sample in range, a sample that does not carry the figure as a number, or a gap of more than two sample periods (between the start and the newest sample, or between two samples).
   - No such run: the count starts at this reading, as before.
   - This is done once per loop (Monitor.guardrail_seeded), whatever it finds.
   - A samples error is a line in the loop's log ("alerts: the guardrails' samples: …; each hold starts at this reading"), and the holds start then.
(3) A sample-based hold estimate, not proof of continuous time out of range (R2, cc-astra A87's wording):
   - A sample says only that the figure was out at that time, so the seeded out-since is never before a sample that saw it out.
   - Samples are hourly, so a dip back into range between two samples is not seen: an old run of samples may join an unobserved recovery and a later relapse. Within one loop the five-minute readings still restart the count as before.
(5) A judged stretch keeps its key (R2, cc-astra A87): the seeding read's window slides (now minus the hold minus two periods), so after a restart the oldest out sample in it is not where a stretch began. A figure whose newest guardrail_out_of_range alert the owner judged while open (its cleared evidence {judged}, read from the alert rows the loop starts with) keeps that alert's out_since_ms, so its key, and is not raised again, unless a sample after that out-since has the figure back in range; only that observed evidence makes a new stretch, seeded from the samples as in (1). A samples error keeps the judged key too (nothing shows the stretch ended). The cost, said plainly: a recovery and relapse the hourly samples did not see, or one older than the window, stays the judged stretch until a reading in range within a loop, or a sample in range, is seen.
(6) Positive evidence only (R3, cc-astra A87, a stale first reading): the judged out-since is not spent at the loop's first reading. It is taken by the first FRESH reading that finds the figure out, whenever that comes, so a first reading where the figure is stale, missing or not collected loses nothing, and a later fresh reading still out goes on with the judged key (no second alert). Only positive evidence ends the judged stretch: a fresh reading with the figure in range (state "in"; "not_collected", "no_range" and a stale figure are no evidence), or a sample in range after the judged out-since (read at the first reading for every judged figure, stale ones too; a figure with no range now has no range a sample could be back within, so no sample is evidence for it). After that, the next stretch out is new and is raised after its own hold. 192.sh (h) checks the parts a black box can reach, each from a restarted loop with only the judged row to go on (hold 15 s): (h1) out from the first reading, no new alert; (h2) no range at the first reading, then out, no new alert; (h3) no range at the first reading, in range at later readings, then out, a new alert; (h4) (R4) out from the first reading, then no range, then out, a new alert. Once taken (R4, rev-g's F1 on R3, the lead's rule (a)), the judged out-since is gone: the stretch lives in the open stretches like any other, so a fresh reading with no range or not collected ends it, and the next fresh reading out starts a new stretch, raised after its own hold. Pinned by the unit test a_taken_judged_stretch_ends_like_any_other and 192.sh (h4). Known difference, not changed here: a restarted loop whose FIRST fresh reading has no range keeps the judged out-since untaken and stays quiet ((h2)), while a loop that never restarted ends the stretch at a no-range reading and raises a new one after its hold. Making restarted and continuous loops agree under "only a fresh reading in range ends it", with 089/092's clear hold in scope, is the lead's follow-up contract. 192.sh's figure is leaked test schemas, read from a scratch test server of its own named by a URL file (as 182's 089.sh), not free disk (R3, the lead 2026-11-16): objective 182 makes free disk a diagnostic with no range, and leaked test schemas raises under storage both on main and with 182, so 192 and 182 land in either order. The stale first reading itself is unit-only: on main no kept group is registered outside the tests (kept::GROUPS is filled only by Group::get, and Group::new is called only in kept.rs's tests), so the binary never says stale for a figure, and the figure 192.sh uses is read at every reading, so a black box cannot make it missing or not collected at the first reading. The unit test a_judged_stretch_survives_a_first_reading_with_no_fresh_figure plays cc-astra's sequence.
(4) Never later than before: the alert fires once the seeded time is a hold old, the same check, key, text and evidence (out_since_ms = the seeded time).

What stays as it is:
- the hold's length and the clear hold;
- which figures alert;
- the alert's key, text and evidence;
- the samples and the sampler;
- GET /api/core-lines.
A figure already open is adopted as before. The clear hold of an adopted alert still restarts with the loop; that delays a clear and never raises one wrongly. It is the named next step.

Store read: host_core_lines(since), the existing read of the trends, through the samples' partial index (spawn_events_host_core_lines on recorded_at_ms), over about 4 hourly samples (raise 2 h plus two periods). It runs once per loop start, so it is not a polled read. Timed on live by rev-e, read only: 12 buffers, 0.12 ms for 7 rows (the 4 h window).
  explain (analyze, buffers) select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('at_ms', s.recorded_at_ms, 'values', s.vals) order by s.recorded_at_ms, s.id), '[]'::jsonb) from (select e.recorded_at_ms, e.id, e.kind -> 'detail' -> 'record' -> 'values' as vals from spawn_events e where e.session_id = 'session_control' and e.event_name = 'control.recorded' and e.kind -> 'detail' -> 'record' ->> 'type' = 'host.core_lines' and e.recorded_at_ms >= (extract(epoch from now()) * 1000)::bigint - 14400000) s

Tests (spawn-cli alerts::guardrails):
- a_figure_out_takes_its_out_since_from_the_newest_unbroken_run_of_samples (new):
  - a run;
  - the newest of two runs;
  - the newest sample in range;
  - a sample without the figure;
  - a gap from the start;
  - a gap between samples;
  - no samples, and samples that are not an array;
  - judged against the current range, not an old one.
- a_restarted_loop_raises_at_the_hold_its_samples_began_not_a_hold_after_the_restart (new):
  - out an hour in the samples: not yet at the restart, then raised at the sample's time + the hold, with that out-since in the key;
  - seeded once: a later reading's samples change nothing;
  - a run broken by a sample in range seeds nothing, and its hold begins at the restart;
  - a samples error is said.
- Every existing guardrails test is unchanged and passes: answers without recent_samples seed nothing.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts/guardrails.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (the flag), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines.rs (reading_with_samples), crates/spawn-cli/src/core_lines_sample.rs (every_ms_from_env). The owner's: rsi/scenarios/192.sh (new).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/192.sh, black box through a real `spawn loop`, `spawn serve` and GET /api/alerts, on a scratch database.
- The ranges file gives leaked test schemas 10^18 or more (its scratch test server counts 0), so it is out at every reading; in range is 0 or more.
- SPAWN_GUARDRAIL_RAISE_SECS=3700: no run of the scenario can wait out the hold from its own start.
- The samples are written by the store's writer (spawn_host_record) and placed in the past.
Eight loop runs, each on its own samples:
(a) one sample out 2.5 h ago, inside the seeding read's window (the hold plus two periods) but more than two periods before the start, a gap: no alert within 20 s of the first reading;
(b) samples out 3 h and 2 h ago, in range 1 h ago: no alert within 20 s;
(d) one sample out 3690 s ago (a seed from it would be a hold old within seconds), the figure in range at the loop's start (a ranges file of 0 or more), then out from a later reading (the file back at 10^18): no open alert 30 s after, since the samples seed once, at the first reading (run before (c), whose open alert a later loop would adopt);
(c) one sample out 3650 s before the loop starts: one open alert within 120 s. Its out_since_ms is that sample's time, it fired at least 3700 s after it, and it fired well before 3700 s after the restart.
(e) (R2, A87) (c)'s alert judged false with `spawn alert judge`; its sample then placed 11000 s ago, outside the next loop's window, and samples out 7000 s and 3600 s ago, with one in range 9000 s ago (before the judged stretch began): no new alert 20 s after the restart. A loop that takes the window's oldest out sample as the start fires at once (7000 s is over the hold);
(f) (R2) samples in range 600 s ago (after the judged stretch began) and out 300 s ago, the hold 60 s for this run: one open alert within 60 s, out since the 300 s sample.
(g) (R2) (f)'s alert cleared by its condition (the figure back in range, the clear hold 2 s for that run), then a sample out 250 s ago, after (f)'s out-since, with none in range since: one open alert within 60 s, out since the 250 s sample. A cleared alert is not a judged stretch.
Without (c)'s alert (a main without 192) (e) to (g) are one failed check, not a harness exit, so 192.sh exits 1 there.
Mutants (R2): judged-ignored dies at (e), break-ignored at (f), break-before-counts at (e) (its in-range sample is from before the judged stretch), condition-counts-as-judged at (g); error-drops-judged dies in the unit test only: the samples read is the same query the reading itself runs first (host_core_lines, a longer window), so a scenario cannot fail it alone.
On the base, (c) gets no alert: the hold starts at the loop's start. 192.sh exits 1 with "(c) … has no guardrail_out_of_range alert 120 s after the start: the hold restarted with the loop". On a9317482 (R1), (e) fires a second alert.
Tests (R2): alerts::guardrails::tests::a_judged_stretch_still_out_after_a_restart_is_not_raised_again (seed, fire, judge false, a Monitor rebuilt from the persisted rows over a slid window: no fire, however long; a samples error: no fire; a sample in range after the stretch began: a new key; one in range before it: no new key; a newest alert cleared by its condition: seeded as before).

Proof: 192-proof.txt (rev-e).

Verified by: the first deploy after landing. Live's days_left (8, against 180 or more) and leaked test schemas (over 200), out since before the deploy, each raise one guardrail_out_of_range alert. They fire 2 h after their first hourly sample out, at the latest one pass after the deploy, instead of never.
